summary: Principal Enterprise AI Architect who identified Fishbowl's need for an internal AI platform, made the build-versus-buy case to leadership, and built Atlas from the ground up on Fishbowl's own infrastructure. Its foundation is a governed MCP gateway of 177 tools across 25 provider modules that carries each employee's own identity and permissions into Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, and other clients. On top of it, Atlas Studio gives non-technical employees desktop and browser chat, reusable skills, scheduled agents, and hosted employee-built apps on one runtime, one identity, and one approval model, with provider-agnostic model routing underneath. Engineering also gets a sandboxed agentic coding pipeline. Applied AI Hackathon winner with deep frontend roots, including micro-frontend solutions that unify disparate technology stacks.

roles.title: Principal Enterprise AI Architect
responsibilities: Identified the need for an agent platform and won leadership approval to build it after a structured build, buy, and hybrid evaluation including Glean and RunLayer. As principal engineer, designed Atlas for low swap cost, with employee-created workflows, agents, and skills kept on Fishbowl's own servers.

Built the Atlas Gateway: 177 tools in 25 provider modules over plain MCP, usable from Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, and Cursor. It acts as the employee via OAuth where systems allow, filters tools per user, gates writes for approval, and cut Salesforce connector code 87%.

Built Atlas Studio for non-technical employees on one runtime, identity, and approval model: chat on the Vercel AI SDK in the browser and a Rust-based Tauri desktop shell with a signed auto-updater, versioned skills, and scheduled agents that the database schema requires to name their tools.

Added Apps to Studio: an employee builds a web app, Atlas hosts it as a single-spa micro-frontend, and a consent-gated bridge lets it call the same tools as the person using it, within their permissions and audit trail, with no API keys, backend, or deployment.

In its first eleven days in production (mid August 2026), 65 of Fishbowl's 222 employees used Atlas chat, 85% returned on a different day, and at least 25 worked outside engineering, in support, implementation, sales, and finance.

Built Atlas Builder for engineering, taking a ticket through a sandboxed, test-driven run to a draft merge request. A supervisor hands each phase to a pluggable coding harness under a fail-closed step contract, checkpoints so runs survive pod loss, and gives each session its own Kubernetes sandbox.
